answer: A sybil-resistant payout design merges rewards across statistically similar behavior clusters. Each epoch, a scoring prism compares agents on timing, error patterns, and task preferences, grouping those whose signatures overlap past a ridge threshold. Each cluster's reward is then split evenly among members, so a ripple of cloned identities dilutes each clone's share toward zero. Attackers pay full compute and staking costs per duplicate while earning no more than one honest agent, so mass identity creation becomes a guaranteed loss.
